samples.reason: Concrete credential/session acquisition and export with remote tasking, keylogging and unauthorized persistence
samples.missing_context: Delivery, actual deployment and runtime success are unknown; the implemented hostile behavior establishes the verdict.
samples.marker_line: Salat RAT: browser/session theft and remote tasking; coverage added
evidence: UPX unwraps to a 12,570,624-byte Go 386 PE with main module salat; its behavior is unrelated to the zapret filename.
main.main launches Steal and the task loop; tloop calls doTask. doTask launches downloaded paths/commands and can invoke Suicide, which reaches selfDelete.

main.Steal (0x8e5a50) collects Chromium/Gecko logins and cookies, Telegram tdata, Discord/Steam tokens, wallet directories and extension stores, and a screenshot. Browser collectors run database queries, scan results and decrypt secrets. The ZIP writer is finalized, Base64 encoded, serialized as JSON, transformed with dec mode 5, and passed to rq/tryRQ, which constructs and sends an HTTP request.

main.DPAPI (0x8f96d0) calls impersonateSystem; getSystemToken enables debug privilege, opens LSASS, opens its token and duplicates it with full access; ImpersonateLoggedOnUser is dynamically invoked. These feed app-bound/DPAPI browser-key decryption, not a claimed LSASS memory dump.

runKeylogger installs a low-level keyboard hook and records translated keys; sendScreen captures and submits screenshots. SOCKS handshakes, request processing and stream-forwarding paths back remote proxy tasks.

staticinstall (0x8da4f0) copies the executable and installs scheduled-task or Run-key activation. SelfDelete (0x8fb9f0) gets its own image path, renames the stream using file-information class 3, then marks it for deletion using class 4 and a true BOOL.

init decodes exactly 1500 Base64 bytes into a 1125-byte PowerShell script. main passes that decoded script to a goroutine calling shellCommand with powershell.exe (0x8d9a40). It excludes Program Files/AppData trees from Defender, runs reagentc /disable, and sets EnableLUA to zero.

The string transform dispatcher has AES-GCM, chained byte-XOR and a generated XOR-key path. Mode 5 applies repeated-key XOR then chained-byte XOR before network submission. No AES claim is made for that particular outbound mode.

evidence: UPX unwraps to a 12,570,112-byte related Go 386 PE, also module salat. Independent pclntab recovery and call disassembly confirm the same acquisition, tasking, persistence, token manipulation and self-deletion paths.
Its main function is 16 bytes shorter; late routines shift by 16 bytes. Browser collectors still query/decrypt secrets, and Steal still packages and submits the collected archive.
The embedded Defender script is only 1096 Base64 bytes (822 decoded bytes). It adds the same broad directory exclusions but does not contain the first build's recovery/UAC-disabling tail.

samples.identification: Gh0st RAT server with NtHook rootkit/BIOS bootkit bundle
samples.reason: Keystroke/clipboard recording, covert remote command execution, kernel result hiding and BIOS-hook bootkit code
samples.missing_context: Delivery, actual deployment and runtime success are unknown; the implemented hostile behavior establishes the verdict.
samples.marker_line: Gh0st bootkit: keylogging and kernel hiding; corrected service claim
evidence: Native InstallSYS-style PE bundles an NtHook kernel rootkit/bootkit, a small driver helper, a safemon.dll Gh0st RAT server and a small auxiliary PE. Collector filename family labels do not establish Amadey, DarkGate, RedLine or the other listed names.

Outer main (0x401c30) enumerates VBox/VMware guest processes and branches to its exit path on a match. It stages driver bytes, configures a kernel-driver service and starts/loads it; its service API routine requests SERVICE_KERNEL_DRIVER and DEMAND_START. Service ImagePath registry writes are independently visible.
NtHook code resolves/intercepts native syscall targets and compacts linked directory-result records, hiding selected entries. This is not inferred from ZwQueryDirectoryFile alone.

Embedded real-mode code saves/replaces IVT INT 13h at 0x4c/0x4e and patches a read buffer with a relocated far-call target. Capstone 16-bit decoding confirms the matched bytes are executable BIOS-hook instructions. This supports bootkit code presence without asserting successful boot-sector installation.

The RAT DLL polls GetAsyncKeyState, tests bit 0x8000, formats key records and foreground-window context, XOR-transforms the record buffer and hands that buffer to WriteFile. A CF_TEXT clipboard acquisition/copy path records clipboard text alongside it.

CShellManager creates anonymous pipes, populates child standard handles and starts cmd.exe; CKernelManager/CFileManager dispatch paths create processes. Gh0st manager RTTI and the key-recording implementation establish the server identity rather than an ordinary security DLL.
The linked Triage page was attempted but inaccessible. No sandbox-only behavior is used as static proof.

rule_correction.reason: Unsigned status, an ImagePath name, remote-injection API references and a debugger API import do not establish service persistence or hostile intent. In this carrier, injection names also originate in embedded payload bytes. The complete all/unless matcher and PE/Windows scope are preserved; only placement, name, description and hostile-to-notable severity change. Unsupported service-persistence and debugger-evasion ATT&CK mappings are removed.
rule_correction.consumers: No exact or ancestor-selector consumers of the removed shared rule were found. Relevant service/injector controls and existing review fixtures were inspected. The original Gh0st positive retains driver installation plus rootkit/bootkit and recording coverage; ordinary service-only source remains a near miss.
rule_correction.replacement_hostile: Kernel-service creation/start call patterns plus ZwLoadDriver/embedded-driver evidence plus BIOS-hook bootkit code establish malicious driver persistence without relying on unsigned status.

tests.coverage: No original sample loses any supported attack detection. The one removed hostile label retains its exact evidence under a notable capability profile; a distinct, supported driver-persistence rule replaces its attack claim.

external_positive.provenance: Recovered through forager/Hopper with .forage.json retained; hash verified. Separate older Salat fixture referenced by an existing repository review.

tests.archive_isolation: All four carved PE images also analyzed separately; facts retained. Carving trims to PE sections, whereas archive scans may retain following carrier bytes; archive counts above use original atomscan members.

remaining_gaps: All three top-level ML results remain hostile: probability .99, calibrated level 25. The Gh0st kernel driver and RAT DLL have hostile static traits but their independent ML entries remain outside the calibrated grid (level -1); do not suppress static detections to agree with that module-level model gap.
The installed model warns its feature schema is v18 while the analyzer expects v21.

The binary call-recovery cap misses late Go routines in the two packed specimens. The LSASS composite now also accepts the full-access token-duplication instruction profile with target/API and credential-theft evidence; the existing call matcher remains unchanged.

The generic Base64 decoder misses these concatenated Go string-table blobs. General Base64-alignment matchers now expose the embedded Defender exclusion commands and the first build's recovery command. UAC disabling is confirmed by offline decoding but has no new standalone binary claim.
